newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan, China, HK to convene business forum.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan, China, HK to convene business forum.

text.p: Entrepreneurs from Taiwan, China and Hong Kong were to meet in Taipei on Monday to discuss economic and trade cooperation, the state-funded Central News Agency reported on Sautrday.

The unofficial economic forum would be the first large-scale contacts across the Taiwan strait after the Taiwan government's November announcement of a freeze on cooperative initiatives with China after Beijing's successful diplomatic courtship of South Africa.
Jing Shuping, chairman of Beijing's All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce, would lead a 22-strong mainland delegation to attend the privately sponsored economic forum, the agency said.
The Chinese delegation, expected to arrive on Sunday, would also hold meetings with Taipei's top negotiator with Beijing, Koo Chen-fu, and prominent Taiwan business leaders, it said.
The meeting was aimed at promoting business ties among Taiwan, China and Hong Kong, and discussing Taiwan investment in the mainland's agriculture, technology and other sectors.
Similar economic forums had been held in Hong Kong and Beijing in 1994 and 1995.
About 30,000 Taiwanese firms have poured more than US$20 billion into China.
Relations between Taipei and Beijing, rivals since a civil war separated them in 1949, nose-dived in November after Beijing's successful courtship of South Africa.
One of the 30 states recognising Taiwan's Republic of China government, South Africa stunned the island on November 27 by announcing it will switch ties from Taipei to Beijing in 1997.
Taipei slammed Beijing's moves as an uncompromising push to drive Taiwan from the international stage.
Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council has said it would not launch further measures to boost economic links with rival China in the near future.
Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui warned in August that the island was becoming too dependent on trade with the mainland and called for limits on local firms' investments in China.
